d: A tough sheet of deep fascia stretched between the ischiopubic rami that separates the deep perineal pouch above from the superficial pouch below; the urethra and vagina pass through it.

The membranous layer of superficial fascia in the perineum. It attaches to the ischiopubic rami and the back edge of the perineal membrane and continues as dartos and Scarpa fascia, which fuses with the fascia lata, so it steers leaked urine forward.
Also called Alcock canal: a tunnel in the obturator fascia on the lateral wall of the ischioanal fossa that carries the pudendal nerve and internal pudendal vessels toward the perineum.
The wavy line in the anal canal where hindgut endoderm met the ectoderm of the anal pit; epithelium, blood supply, nerves and lymph drainage all change across it.
The fibromuscular center of the perineum between the anal canal and the vagina or penile bulb, where the perineal muscles and the external anal sphincter anchor; deeper obstetric lacerations tear it.

A connection between portal and caval veins. At the anorectal junction the superior rectal veins (portal) meet the middle and inferior rectal veins (caval), so in portal hypertension blood diverts there and swells rectal varices. Other sites are the lower esophagus and the umbilicus.

The first lymph node that receives drainage from a tumor. It is found with blue dye or a radiotracer and biopsied; if it is free of cancer, a full lymph node dissection can usually be avoided. It is used in vulvar, penile and breast cancer.
